title: Strain-tunable charge localization coupled to complex magnetic orders in EuAl$_4$
authors: M. Baumgartner, Xunyang Hong, Tianren Wang, Fazhi Yang, Yuetong Wu, Junzhang Ma, Tian Shang, J. Oppliger, J. Küspert, M. Hücker, O. Ivashko, F. Igoa Saldaña, M. v. Zimmermann, S. Pyon, K. Kudo, M. Nohara, P. Sačer, A. Akrap, N. Barišić, M. Novak, Qisi Wang, J. Chang
abstract: Charge localization is particularly interesting when coupled to antiferromagnetic spin structures. Coupled spin-charge orders are well established in elemental chromium and correlated oxide superconductors, yet the interplay between charge order and more complex magnetic textures -- such as skyrmion lattices and chiral spin structures -- remains largely unexplored. Here we report a comprehensive study of how charge localization couples to the unusually rich sequence of magnetic phases in EuAl$_4$. Using x-ray diffraction under applied magnetic field and uniaxial pressure, we demonstrate a direct coupling between the charge and spin order parameters. In the absence of external stimuli, charge localization is markedly enhanced upon entering the magnetically ordered phases. Strikingly, this effect is highly susceptible to strain: uniaxial pressure applied along the charge-order propagation direction further enhances localization, whereas pressure applied perpendicular to it weakens it. Application of magnetic field reveals both competitive and possible collaborative interactions between spin and charge ordering.This flexible coupling between spin and charge ordering opens a new route to designing symmetry-breaking states. Chiral charge order may for example be patterned from spin structures with that symmetry.
summary: This work comprehensively studies the interplay between charge localization and complex magnetic orders in EuAl4 using high-energy X-ray diffraction. By applying uniaxial strain and magnetic fields, the researchers demonstrated that this coupling is highly sensitive to the symmetry of the applied stress. The findings reveal a new route for controlling electronic states by manipulating the underlying spin structure.
main_problem: The study investigates how charge localization couples to complex magnetic orders, such as skyrmion lattices or chiral spin structures, in the material EuAl4.
main_result: The coupling between spin and charge order is highly tunable by external stimuli; uniaxial strain along the charge-order propagation direction enhances localization, while perpendicular strain weakens it.
method: High-energy X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements were performed under applied magnetic fields and controlled uniaxial pressures to probe structural changes related to electronic ordering.
model_or_system: The physical system is the compound EuAl4, which exhibits both charge density wave (CDW) behavior and rich sequences of antiferromagnetic spin structures. The analysis focuses on quantifying the degree of charge localization through harmonic satellite reflections.
key_observables: Charge localization parameters ($\eta_{21}, \eta_{31}$), charge incommensurability ($\delta$), and structural Bragg peak shifts used to quantify strain.
important_parameters: Applied uniaxial pressure (along/perpendicular to CDW propagation) and external magnetic field strength ($B$).
main_assumptions: The coupling mechanism is assumed to be rooted in degrees of freedom residing on the same Eu site, suggesting it goes beyond conventional electron-phonon coupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate temperature dependence of charge ordering harmonics ($\eta_{i0}$) under varying strain and magnetic fields, demonstrating how external parameters modulate the spin-charge coupling strength.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the experimental methodology using XRD to measure structural changes (strain) and electronic order (CDW satellites). It then systematically explores the interplay by measuring charge localization as a function of temperature, uniaxial strain, and magnetic field, concluding with implications for designing symmetry-breaking states.
why_interesting: The direct tunability of charge/spin coupling via mechanical strain provides an experimental playground to study emergent quantum phases, which is relevant for understanding correlated electron physics in novel materials.
